about: Every number this video shows or says, with its source. Checked by the facts gate against the source pages; from video/studio/research/runs/2026-10-28-script-playbook.md (example 3) and re-read on each source page on Oct 28, 2026.

servicetitan.title: State of the Trades: Top Performer Profile
servicetitan.topDefinition: contractors in the 90th percentile of revenue within their trade and market segment
servicetitan.quote: On 57% of residential jobs, top performers present good-better-best proposals ... The rest do this on 41% of residential jobs.
servicetitan.method: internal analysis of aggregated, anonymized data from participating ServiceTitan customers, trailing 12 months through January 2026; metrics describe behaviors correlated with higher performance

menu.title: The compromise effect in action: Lessons from a restaurant's menu
menu.authors: Pia Pinger, Isabel Ruhmer-Krell, Heiner Schumacher
menu.journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
menu.quote: an option that becomes a compromise gains on average five percentage points in market share (introduction); abstract: gain on average five percent in market share
menu.highEnd: The compromise effect tends to be bigger when adding a choice at the high end than at the low end.

acca.title: Survey reveals strategies to boost HVAC close rates by double digits
acca.study: Contractor of the Future (ACCA and Farmington Consulting Group)
acca.quote: Contractors offering four or more options see their closing rate jump by 10 percentage points to 52% ... 42% when offering one, two, or three options.
acca.caveat: The survey groups one, two and three options together, so it does not compare one option with three. Correlational, HVACR sample.

gbb.good: The job done right. Nothing extra.
gbb.better: What you'd pick for your own house.
gbb.best: Plus upgrades: longer warranty, faster start date.
gbb.note: tiers and single are the lesson itself (good, better, best is three prices; the habit it replaces is one price), not findings
